note: The sensible bot (tools/bot.mjs) on seeds 1-3 for 8 sim hours (two game days: the clock runs six times faster than the sim) from a fresh game. Proposed from the first run on 8 Oct 2026 at 48 game hours and re-proposed on 8 Oct 2026 when sim seconds became real seconds (the clock six times faster than motion): the same money a real minute, but a quicker start and fewer lost, since a peak lasts a sixth of the sim seconds it did while patience and platform caps are in sim seconds; and lost re-proposed on 11 Oct 2026 when trains began boarding through their stop (two doors a car, 0.7 passengers a second each) instead of all at once on arrival: people who reach the platform while a train stands now catch it, so Stockport's queue rarely reaches its cap and lost fell from about 155 to 30 while cash and milestones stayed in range. Re-proposed again on 11 Oct 2026 when stations began as halts (the owner's decision): Stockport's subway, platform 3 and booking hall come before the second unit (0.17 to 0.4 h), so Heaton Chapel comes later (0.4 to 0.72 h) and everything after a little later; stages cost money, so less cash at the end; and peaks bite again (lost 30 to 205), as the second unit arrives later and Stockport's subway brings more people in. Lost re-proposed on 12 Oct 2026 when demand came from door-to-door journey times (docs/DESIGN.md, Journeys): each group draws its own time budget and gives up when its wait has used what's left, so the peaks press on Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme too when full trains leave Stockport (205 to about 350, a third of it beyond Stockport); demand is scaled so the milestones stay where they were (Heaton Chapel 0.72 to 0.65 h, Ardwick 5.55 to 5.2 h). Re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when trains began running to a timetable (docs/DESIGN.md, Timetable): the units now keep an even gap instead of running wherever they were added, so waits are what the journeys assume and far fewer give up (lost about 350 to 80, nearly all at Stockport's first morning, before the second unit); stops overrun when a crowded train meets a crowded platform, but by the second morning the bot's line has the room, so its trains run at most half a minute late. The bot also buys the faster timetable once it has £45,000 spare (a player would, rather than sit on the money), which takes about £20,000 off cash at the end on main too; cash at the end re-proposed to 25,000-55,000 for both. New measures: the share of main-line departures within five minutes of the timetable, the worst lateness in minutes, and the longest daytime quiet (06:00-22:00 with nothing bought, 0.7 h on main). Lost re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when the peaks were made to press again (docs/DESIGN.md, Journeys and Platforms; the owner asked for pressure at the stations they buy): no grace past the budget, and a wait past the timetabled gap felt at three times riding, with demand 1.9 to 1.95 so the milestones stay where they were; lost about 80 to 200, nearly 40% of it beyond Stockport (a new measure, lost beyond home %, 33-100; 11, 8 and 12% on seeds 1-3 before), most at Heaton Chapel and Levenshulme in the second morning. Platforms now block, but on the bot's line never engage. The owner agrees ranges when the pacing is settled. `ok` is inside the range, `near` within 15% of it, `off` beyond. Lost and lost beyond home % re-proposed on 12 October 2026 when taxi ranks came (docs/DESIGN.md, Taxi ranks): a share of those who give up at a station with a rank take a cab while one's in, counted as by cab rather than lost, so lost falls (about 200 to 140) and more of it is Stockport's first morning, before the bot can afford a rank (beyond home 38 to 28%); lost re-proposed as 120-300 and beyond home as 25-100, and by cab added at 15-60 (about 32). The bot buys a rank once a dozen have given up at a station, so Stockport's comes just after the second unit and Heaton Chapel a little later (0.65 to 0.75 h). Things going wrong came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Things going wrong): failed trains and signal failures from the second sim hour, one or two in 8 sim hours, with replacement buses and a spare unit the bot buys once a train has failed. The milestones held; what moved is where trouble lands, the second morning's peak on seeds 2 and 3, mostly as Stockport's platform fills behind a held train: lost 139 to about 210 (seed 2's two failed trains 300), cash 50,800 to about 40,300, worst late up to 8 minutes, and lost beyond home 28 to 23%, so that range is re-proposed as 15-100. New measures, proposed: failures 0-3 and signal failures 0-3 a run, and lost in trouble (who gave up while something was wrong or in the quarter hour after) 0-200. Trouble softened the same day: nothing starts where it would still be going in a peak's busiest hour (troubleCalm, 06:30-08:30 and 16:00-18:00 by the clock), as seed 2 lost 162 people and seed 11 a quarter of its takings to failures in the second morning. On seeds 1-12 the most any seed earns less than the same seed with no trouble is 8.5% of its cash at the end (25.6% before); on seeds 1-3 lost in trouble 1, 162, 81 to 1, 42, 33 and cash 40,300 to 48,600 on average (seed 2 still buys the spare unit after its one failure). Lost in trouble re-proposed as 0-150 (124 the most on seeds 1-12). Homes and draw came from Census 2021 the same day (docs/DESIGN.md, Homes and draw), scaled so Stockport's morning trips to Piccadilly are as before; Stockport's real draw is half the guess and Piccadilly's homes well under it, so the evenings earned less and Levenshulme slipped past the first night (2.3 to 4.0 h), and fareMult went from 12 to 13.5 to bring it back (2.6 h). Heaton Chapel 0.75 to 0.63 h, Ardwick 4.9 to 4.8 h, lost about the same (150 to 193), and cash at the end 48,600 to 58,600 with the dearer fares, so cash at the end is re-proposed as 25,000-65,000. Homes that grow came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Homes that grow): each owned station's homes grow towards a ceiling from the census at 6% of the gap a sim hour times the reach of its trip, and demand reads them. Growth at 12% took cash at the end to 73,500 (off), so it was halved to keep the opening as it was: on seeds 1-3 Levenshulme 2.6 h (as before), Ardwick 4.8 to 5.0 h (seed 1's one failed train lands in the second morning now, 5.5 h), cash 58,600 to 55,500, boarded 4,630 to 4,660, lost 193 to 280 (seed 1's failure, 408; seeds 2 and 3 235 and 198); on seeds 1-12 the means move little (Levenshulme 2.9 to 2.7 h, cash 54,400 to 58,800, lost 189 to 221, lost in trouble 30 to 48). Over 30 sim hours Piccadilly comes at 8.6-9.3 h (9.2 h before) and Hazel Grove at 13.6-13.8 h (14.0 h). New measure, homes grown (homes over the census catchments at the end, about 130 in 8 sim hours, 580 in 30), proposed as 80-200. Weather and seasons came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Weather and seasons): spells from the weather's own seeded random numbers, so the rest of the game's dice are as they were (the bot's --fair, the weather unfelt, matches main exactly); rain makes the walk and an open wait feel a little longer, snow slows the line and keeps a few at home, leaves slow autumn's trains. The first game day stays dry, as rain in seed 2's first evening took Levenshulme past the first night (2.62 to 3.75 h); with it dry the milestones hold on seeds 1-3 (Ardwick 5.0 to 4.8 h, as seed 1's failed train no longer lands in the second morning), cash 55,500 to 62,300, lost 280 to 209. On seeds 1-12 boarded 4,730 to 4,721 and cash 58,800 to 61,100 (where trouble lands moves more than the rain). Over 32 sim hours, a whole year, cash at the end is 6% under the same seeds unfelt and boarded 4%, wet about a fifth of the time. New measure, wet hours (sim hours of rain or snow), proposed as 0-2.5 in 8 sim hours (1.0, 0.48, 0.48 on seeds 1-3). Every platform in use came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Platforms and Expresses): each service takes the platforms it really uses, a turning list shared out by unit (the stoppers turn in Stockport's 4 and 3 by turns), and Avanti West Coast and CrossCountry call at Stockport once platform 3 is built and pay an access charge (£40) and £2 a long-distance passenger. Against main with the weather, on seeds 1-3: Levenshulme 2.6 to 2.5 h, Ardwick 4.8 h as before, lost 209 to 180, and cash at the end 62,300 to 65,900, just over its range (the expresses pay about £3,000 of it, and buy Levenshulme a little sooner), so cash at the end is re-proposed as 25,000-70,000; the trains' platforms change nothing else the bot sees, as the units keep their gap. New measures, proposed: express £ (what the expresses paid) 2,000-5,000, and through (long-distance passengers on and off at owned stations) 500-1,200. Car parks and bus links came on 12 October 2026 (docs/DESIGN.md, Car parks and bus links): the census's pools beyond a walk travel by car or bus once a car park or bus link is built, and the bot buys them before a morning once it has twice the price. Nothing changes until one is built (the milestones to Levenshulme are as on main); in 8 sim hours the bot builds Levenshulme's bus stop and car park in the second morning and Stockport's car park in the third, so Ardwick comes a little later (4.8 to 5.1 h), cash at the end falls (65,900 to 39,200, the money in car parks), boarded rises (4,770 to 4,830) and the longest quiet stretch shortens (2.1 to 1.5 h, so that range is re-proposed as 1.2-2.7). New measures, proposed: by car (drivers who parked) 30-200 and by bus link 20-150.
